A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ProAct benchmark and framework. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–F are readable and can be matched across pagination and numbering changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, component ablations, trajectory simulations, and appendix analyses of hyperparameters, cross-view generalization, and latency.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds projection-head experiments, trigger-error measurements, representation analyses, and actor-held-out evaluation.

M1.justification: The proposed HBM losses, entropy-based planner, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Projection heads are tested as alternative ablation variants, not adopted into ProAct-Helper. The rollout safeguard discussed in v3 Section 6.4 already appears in v1 Appendix A.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ProAct-75 collection, 75 tasks, three application scenarios, and constituent video sources. The added actor-held-out experiment repartitions existing self-collected videos; it does not introduce new data or task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 Table 4 adds two evaluated comparison variants using MLP projection heads with dimensions 128 and 256. The external-model comparators and existing plain-model and greedy comparisons in Tables 1–3 are unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 adds training on Actors 1–4 and testing on Actor 5 against a full-data reference, FPR/FNR evaluation, and representation diagnostics with shuffled-pair controls. Projection-head experiments reuse the existing stratified mini-split. These substantially expand evaluation procedures while retaining the original main-experiment settings.

E4.justification: New Appendix B analyses test projection-head utility, under-triggering versus over-triggering, pair-specific representation alignment versus collapse, and actor generalization. These extend v1's component ablations, hyperparameter sensitivity, cross-view tests, and qualitative failure analyses, which are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new shuffled-pair analysis is a representation control, not an uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Existing Tables 1–3 and v1 Tables 4–5, now v3 Tables 8 and 10, retain identical values. New Tables 4–7 and 9 add substantial diagnostic results. For example, the new actor experiment reports Step F1 of 34.97 under actor-held-out training versus 89.97 under full-data training; these are different settings, not a version-to-version performance decline.

T1.justification: Appendix B.4 newly defines SSO50 as the fraction of task-representation variance explained by the top 50 principal components of trigger representations. This is a limited mathematical diagnostic definition. The task-graph definitions, binding losses, entropy formulation, and existing metric equations remain unchanged, with no new proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same benchmark, HBM-plus-planning framework, and headline performance claims. The added introduction sentence distinguishing proactive judgment from action recognition clarifies the existing scope.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive interpretations of projection-head optimization, pair-specific alignment without representation collapse, and weaker fine-grained generalization across actors. Its Impact Statement also explicitly limits deployment applicability and discusses false-positive intervention risks, calibrated thresholds, and human confirmation.

D1.justification: v3 specifies the new projection heads' Linear–ReLU–Linear architecture, hidden size 2048, and projection dimensions, and clarifies consent and anonymization practices. Conversely, Section 6.4 drops v1's explicit description of simulated human branch-switching after robot preemption. Existing training settings, prompts, and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations concerning video representations, label-distribution learning, and multi-agent world models, while removing Premack and Woodruff and Rabinowitz et al. The research positioning remains largely unchanged. Several other reference changes merely update publication details for existing works.

P1.justification: Changes include localized grammar corrections, updated affiliations and publication text, a conflict-of-interest disclosure, expanded impact discussion, and additional Appendix B subsections. Section 6.4 summarizes an existing appendix safeguard; the overall section sequence and most established prose are retained.

P2.justification: Five new tables, v3 Tables 4–7 and 9, substantially expand the quantitative presentation. Existing displays and the task-graph gallery are retained and repositioned. Figure 4 corrects pooled versus unpooled representation labels, example photographs receive anonymization, and headers and float placement change.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's existing ablations and cross-view tests, v3 provides useful additional controls for HBM and exposes a substantial actor-generalization limitation. Clearer deployment boundaries improve interpretation. These are incremental quality gains: actor generalization is tested on one held-out individual, uncertainty remains unreported, and the simulated human policy is slightly less explicit.
